clue.text: Store form of isotope in desert

indicators.note: a form of a word is a reshaped version of it, so its letters are rearranged
one piece is placed in the other, which wraps around it

blocks.note: a desert is dry, arid land
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A chemist stashes some form of isotope out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' is the adjective, as in desert island, so it means DRY rather than a sandy place.
explanation.definitionFit: A depository is a building or place where goods are kept safely, a warehouse.

clue.text: Nonsense — boast of bigamist?

blocks.note: first meaning: unintelligible talk, gibberish
second meaning, whimsical: Dutch is old Cockney slang for a wife, so a bigamist could brag of having two

explanation.surface: Gibberish, says a man bragging about having two wives.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'my old Dutch' (from duchess) is a man's wife, so a bigamist has double the Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for speech or writing that is completely incomprehensible gibberish.

clue.text: Hand in part penning second song

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, as livestock in a pen, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the palm is part of the hand
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A hand in a card game, part of which involves writing a second song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand in part' looks like a card hand; read it as the part of your hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is a sacred song or hymn, especially one from the biblical Book of Psalms.

clue.text: Over everyone, small earwigs and beetles primarily creep

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is over comes higher, so the earlier pieces sit above the word for everyone
primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letters count

blocks.note: slim means small, as in slim chances
the opening letters of earwigs and beetles
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A list of small insects, earwigs and beetles, crawling all over everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creep' looks like a verb for the insects, but it is the noun for an unpleasant person.
explanation.definitionFit: A slimeball is slang for a repellent, obsequious person, which is what a creep is.

clue.text: Soldier drunk, other ranks caught up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top, backwards
something caught is held inside, so one piece is trapped within the other

blocks.note: a toper is a heavy drinker, a drunk
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A soldier is drunk and the other ranks are caught up in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier, especially one in a cavalry or armoured regiment.

clue.text: Rash having two drinks, don’t start the second

indicators.note: not starting means the opening letter of the later drink is left off

blocks.note: rosé is pink wine, the first drink
cola is a fizzy soft drink, the second drink

explanation.surface: Someone breaks out in a rash after two drinks and is warned off a second.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseola is a rose-coloured skin eruption, especially a viral one seen in young children.

clue.text: Some knitting order a pain

blocks.note: the Order of the Garter is the senior English order of chivalry
a stitch is a sharp pain in the side

explanation.surface: Knitting to order is a real pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The knitting suggests stitches, but STITCH comes from the pain, and GARTER from the Order of the Garter, Britain's oldest order of knighthood.
explanation.definitionFit: Garter stitch is the simplest knitting pattern, made by knitting every row, so it is one kind of knitting.

clue.text: A law on mummification finally accepted by Roman ruler, not head of ancient Egypt

indicators.note: on here means placed next to, so the pieces follow one another
finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept
without its head, the word loses its first letter
a thing accepted by another is taken inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
lex is the Latin for law
Hadrian was a Roman emperor
the closing letter of mummification

explanation.surface: A legal decree about mummification approved by a Roman emperor who was not ruling Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not head' belongs with the Roman ruler, leaving 'of ancient Egypt' as the definition rather than part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandrian describes things belonging to Alexandria, the great city founded on the Egyptian coast in antiquity.

clue.text: Rubbish match for a Scottish vegetable

blocks.note: tat is cheap, worthless stuff
a tie is a match in a cup competition

explanation.surface: A poor football match fit only for a Scottish vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattie is the Scots word for a potato, the staple vegetable of tatties and neeps.

clue.text: Call to keep oven hot

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the outer word holds the inner one

blocks.note: to ring is to call on the telephone
an oast is a kiln, an oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: A call to leave the oven on so it stays hot.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is the kiln used to dry hops, a familiar sight in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: Roasting is an informal intensifier for very hot weather or conditions, as in a roasting day.

clue.text: Putting it mildly, a Trappist’s remit?

blocks.note: first meaning: understating the case
second meaning, whimsical: Trappist monks keep near-silence, so their brief is to speak as little as possible

explanation.surface: Understating it, a monk's job description.
explanation.walkthrough: Trappists are a Catholic order known for keeping silence, so saying the least is literally their remit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom used to admit an understatement, meaning the reality is more extreme.

clue.text: Devastating thing having ruined a trick

blocks.note: something torn is ruined, damaged
taken as written
to do someone is to trick or swindle them

explanation.surface: A devastating thing has spoilt a magician's trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm that wrecks everything in its narrow path.

clue.text: Sumo like this is so without mercy

blocks.note: surface reading: a remark about how sumo wrestling is conducted
setter's reading: take the middle letters out of the word sumo and you are left with the word so

explanation.surface: Sumo wrestling done this way is truly merciless.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMO with its heart (UM) removed is SO, so sumo treated heartlessly is so; the answer describes that operation and also means cruelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting heartlessly means acting cruelly, with no compassion or pity shown to anyone.

clue.text: Honey in soft centre?

blocks.note: sweet can mean gentle or soft, as in a sweet voice
the heart is the centre of something

explanation.surface: Honey found in a chocolate with a soft centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey and sweetheart are both affectionate terms of address for a loved partner.

clue.text: As one man is on, two union leaders off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

the leader of union is its first letter, taken twice

explanation.surface: A strike ballot: everyone is on board except two union bosses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two union leaders' is two copies of the first letter of union, added to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as one means acting in complete agreement, with every member of a group concurring.

clue.text: Pull away from wife and sleep

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
rest is sleep or repose

explanation.surface: Someone drags themselves away from their wife and their sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrest something is to pull it away forcibly with a twisting movement.

clue.text: Country cutting an American test

indicators.note: cutting something trims it short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article, A

a trial is a test

explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' reads like a verb acting on the country; it trims the last letter off the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a landlocked nation in central Europe whose capital is Vienna.

clue.text: Corrupt lot parliament, pure down-and-outs

indicators.note: something corrupt is debased and twisted, so these letters are distorted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

clue.text: Cause of ferment, Irish poet turning tail

indicators.note: turning the tail round means its last letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet

explanation.surface: An Irish poet stirring up trouble then running away.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the tail of the poet's name, its last two letters, turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus that converts sugars into alcohol and gas, which is fermentation.

clue.text: Does loveless couple give up hope?

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, so loveless means without that letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A couple whose love has died wonder whether to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, used here as a verb matching the clue's question.

clue.text: Strong flavour merits pan being given a stir

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cook says a pan with a strong flavour deserves a stir.

clue.text: Inside scrapheap hid some bugs

indicators.note: inside means within, so the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: spanning the end of scrapheap, all of hid and the start of some

explanation.surface: Someone hid some bugs inside a scrapheap.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are small sap-sucking insects such as greenfly, and bugs is a looser word for insects.

clue.text: Taking hour to go in, hospital department has one seat

indicators.note: going in means being placed inside the other letters

blocks.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
taken as written
HR is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A hospital department waits an hour for a seat to come free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' is the verb here, to install someone in a position.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthrone a monarch or bishop is to formally place them on a throne, to seat them.

clue.text: Sort of a perch right to feed baby

indicators.note: feeding puts something into a mouth, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
to perch is to sit
wee is Scottish for small, babyish
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sort of perch for feeding the baby, like a high chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baby' is an adjective here, meaning tiny, as in a baby carrot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning in a manner of speaking, roughly, so to speak.

clue.text: In brief, run is for trainer

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, which surrounds it

blocks.note: to brief someone is to tell them
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written

explanation.surface: In short, a jog is good for someone's fitness coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In brief' looks like 'in short'; read it as the run going into a verb meaning brief.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice frame that climbing plants are trained along, so it trains them.

clue.text: Track I’d sing out of tune

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

clue.text: Sign drenched clothes most worn out

clue.text: Success securing wire to become less convincing

clue.text: Son isn’t wearing any trousers

clue.text: Face piece, knowing pottery

clue.text: What a stone being catapulted is, for sure

definitions.text: What a stone being catapulted is

blocks.clueFragment: What a stone being catapulted is

explanation.surface: A stone flung from a catapult is certainly something.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the phrase into its two adjectives and it describes a stone in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard and fast rules are definite and fixed, not open to exception or doubt.

clue.text: Acknowledging limitations, this train’s last stop?

blocks.note: first meaning: true only up to a point
second meaning, whimsical: the farthest point a train travels to

explanation.surface: A rail announcement that this train terminates here.

clue.text: Not in Italy, a flying race

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

clue.text: A row I stomach, concealing bit of a pout for one always

taken as written

clue.text: Post-watershed screening time ultimately spoiled

the closing letter of time

clue.text: Netting second of goals, Man United playing with spirit

indicators.note: the second of a word is its second letter

a net catches and holds something inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

the second letter of goals

clue.text: Sporting event returning live, though somewhat on the periphery

clue.text: Train a girl until fluent in three languages

clue.text: Drennan’s country remedies all rubbished

the closing letter of programme
